skill.name: gh-cli
skill.description: Reference skill for GitHub CLI commands across repositories, issues, pull requests, Actions, projects, releases, gists, Codespaces, authentication, and API usage.
skill.summary: Use GitHub CLI commands for repositories, pull requests, Actions, releases, and Codespaces.
skill.author: github

security_audit.summary: The analyzer matched many Markdown command examples and code fences in SKILL.md; most are false positives for executable code, private key access, or reconnaissance. Confirmed risks are limited to privileged installation commands and GitHub token handling examples that could expose credentials if an agent runs them without explicit user approval. No prompt injection attempt or hidden exfiltration intent was found.

remediation.issue: Privileged installation commands are included in the skill text.
remediation.suggestion: Replace sudo install snippets with links to official GitHub CLI installation documentation, or require explicit user confirmation before suggesting them.

remediation.issue: Token examples print or export active GitHub credentials.
remediation.suggestion: Remove gh auth token display examples or add clear redaction guidance and warnings before any token command is suggested.

remediation.issue: Bulk GitHub operations can modify many issues, pull requests, or projects.
remediation.suggestion: Add dry-run, listing, and confirmation steps before examples that close, delete, merge, transfer, or edit resources in bulk.

content.user_title: Manage GitHub from the Command Line
content.value_statement: GitHub teams need fast command guidance for repositories, issues, pull requests, Actions, and releases. This skill supplies focused gh CLI examples and workflows for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
actual_capabilities: Maps common GitHub tasks to gh CLI commands and flags.
Covers repositories, issues, pull requests, Actions, projects, releases, gists, and Codespaces.
Shows authentication, configuration, alias, extension, and shell completion workflows.
Includes REST and GraphQL request patterns through gh api.
Provides automation patterns using JSON output, jq filters, pagination, and aliases.
Documents troubleshooting, exit codes, environment variables, and help commands.
limitations: It is a reference skill; it does not execute commands by itself.
Examples may require local gh installation, authentication, and repository permissions.
Some operations can change repositories, projects, releases, or account settings.
Version details can become outdated as GitHub CLI changes.

use_cases.title: Repository Maintenance
use_cases.description: Find commands to create repositories, update settings, manage labels, and inspect repository metadata.

use_cases.title: Pull Request Operations
use_cases.description: Build gh CLI flows for listing, reviewing, merging, and checking pull requests.

use_cases.title: Automation and Releases
use_cases.description: Use Actions, releases, API calls, and JSON output to support repeatable GitHub workflows.

prompt_templates.title: Find a Repository Command
prompt_templates.prompt: Show the gh CLI command to view repository details for owner/repo. Include required flags and a short explanation.

prompt_templates.title: Review Pull Requests
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me list open pull requests in owner/repo that need my review. Use gh CLI and include useful filters.

prompt_templates.title: Automate a Release
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a gh CLI workflow to create a release from tag v1.2.3, attach release notes, and verify the result.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Safe GitHub Changes
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a safe gh CLI sequence for updating repository settings, managing labels, and checking workflow runs. Include confirmation points before destructive commands.

output_examples.input: I need to find pull requests waiting for my review.
output: Suggested gh CLI search for open pull requests assigned to your review queue.
Includes filters for repository, state, reviewer, and output fields.
Notes which commands only read data and which commands change review state.

output_examples.input: Help me prepare a GitHub release from an existing tag.
output: Step-by-step release plan using gh release commands.
Includes checks for tag existence, release notes, asset upload, and final verification.
Calls out the confirmation step before publishing the release.

output_examples.input: I need to inspect a failed GitHub Actions run.
output: Workflow triage commands for listing runs, viewing jobs, and reading logs.
Explains how to narrow results by branch, event, status, and workflow name.

best_practices: Confirm repository, owner, and branch before running commands that modify GitHub resources.
Use scoped tokens and avoid printing tokens in chat, terminals, or logs.
Request dry runs or list commands before delete, close, merge, release, or transfer actions.
anti_patterns: Do not run destructive gh commands from generated output without reviewing the target resources.
Do not paste real GitHub tokens into prompts or commit them to files.
Do not use privileged install commands unless the user approved system changes.

faq.question: Does this skill execute gh commands automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides command guidance. Execution depends on the host tool, user permissions, and explicit approvals.

faq.question: What GitHub areas are covered?
faq.answer: It covers repositories, issues, pull requests, Actions, projects, releases, gists, Codespaces, authentication, and API access.

faq.question: Can it help with GitHub Enterprise?
faq.answer: Yes. The reference includes hostname options for GitHub Enterprise, but users must supply their own host details.

faq.question: What access is required?
faq.answer: Commands require a configured gh CLI session and GitHub permissions for the target resource.

faq.question: Is it safe to use with tokens?
faq.answer: Use caution. Avoid printing tokens, use scoped credentials, and redact secrets from prompts and logs.

faq.question: Does it cover API calls?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes gh api patterns for REST and GraphQL requests.
